conversations.title: Attendance is not lasting employment improvement
conversations.setting: The lesson's program reports 200 workshop attendees but has not measured follow-up employment outcomes.
turns: Program manager
Two hundred people attended our workshops. The draft calls that proof of lasting employment improvement.
Evaluation officer
Attendance is an output: it tells us what the program delivered, not what happened afterward.
Program manager
Then an outcome would concern a change in participants' circumstances rather than simply their presence?
Evaluation officer
Exactly. We haven't measured follow-up employment outcomes, so the lasting-improvement claim goes beyond our evidence.
Program manager
How does the theory of change fit into this distinction for the board discussion?
Evaluation officer
It explains how we expect activities to contribute to our mission. It doesn't prove that contribution occurred.
Program manager
So we can explain the intended link between workshops and employment without claiming the link has been demonstrated.
Evaluation officer
Yes. Keep the observed attendance figure and the intended outcome in separate sentences.
Program manager
I'll revise the spoken update to report attendance and identify the missing follow-up information.
Evaluation officer
Good. That recognizes delivered work while making clear what we still need to learn about outcomes.

conversations.title: Food parcels and household stability
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a community organization distributed 300 food parcels this month; no information on longer-term household stability has been collected.
turns: Community program lead
We distributed three hundred parcels. Can our presentation describe that as three hundred households becoming stable?
Learning coordinator
No. Parcel distribution is an output, and the count doesn't establish either unique households or lasting stability.
Community program lead
I see two gaps: recipients may repeat, and receiving a parcel doesn't itself measure the longer-term outcome.
Learning coordinator
Correct. Our mission may include household stability, but we need an appropriate measure of that change.
Community program lead
Could we explain the parcels as an immediate activity within our theory of change instead?
Learning coordinator
Yes. Say how the activity is intended to help without claiming unmeasured results.
Community program lead
I'll use parcels distributed as the label, rather than families transformed or another unsupported description.
Learning coordinator
That will make the figure easier to interpret and avoid overstating what the program knows.
Community program lead
Let's discuss what follow-up would be useful and proportionate before making another impact claim.
Learning coordinator
Agreed. We'll distinguish the delivery record from any future evidence about participant outcomes.

conversations.title: A mentoring match is the start, not the result
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a youth mentoring project has made twenty matches; meetings and participant outcomes have not yet been tracked.
turns: Mentoring coordinator
Twenty mentoring matches are in place. Is that an outcome we can present to the donor?
Program designer
It is a useful delivery milestone, but it doesn't show whether mentoring meetings happened or participants benefited.
Mentoring coordinator
So the match is part of the activity pathway, and improvement would need separate evidence?
Program designer
Exactly. The theory of change describes the expected steps between matching people and the intended benefit.
Mentoring coordinator
Would saying the project created twenty successful mentoring relationships still overstate what we know?
Program designer
Yes. We haven't tracked meetings or defined relationship success, so that label adds an unsupported conclusion.
Mentoring coordinator
I'll say twenty matches were made and explain that engagement and outcomes remain to be assessed.
Program designer
Good. We should choose follow-up questions that respect participants and fit the program's purpose.
Mentoring coordinator
Then the donor update can celebrate the setup milestone without turning it into evidence of lasting change.
Program designer
Precisely. Clear distinctions help us discuss progress honestly and identify the next learning need.

additional_scenario.title: Downloads recorded; use and outcomes unknown
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional nonprofit's budgeting guide has 500 downloads. The organization has no information on unique readers, use of the guide, or changed financial behavior. Explain the output and intended outcome without giving financial advice.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the program communications lead. Explain what the download count actually measures.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the learning officer. Ask how use and outcomes would differ from downloads.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Five hundred downloads show distribution activity, not five hundred confirmed changes in financial behavior.
additional_scenario.complication: A donor asks you to describe all downloads as people helped.
success_checks: Distinguish downloads, users, and outcomes.
Explain the intended mission connection without claiming proof.
Identify a proportionate follow-up question rather than invent a result.

conversations.title: Check the award before moving funds
conversations.setting: The lesson's team proposes moving grant money to another activity, but the award restrictions have not been checked.
turns: Program lead
We want to move some grant money to another activity. Could you clarify whether the award permits that?
Grants manager
I need to check the award terms. We haven't established whether this is restricted funding for the original activity.
Program lead
The new activity supports our mission. Doesn't that make the change acceptable within the grant?
Grants manager
Mission fit matters, but it doesn't establish permission to change a funded deliverable or spending category.
Program lead
Then which documents should we review before presenting the transfer as an available option?
Grants manager
The award terms and approved budget, along with any applicable change process or donor correspondence.
Program lead
Could you confirm whether the proposal requires permission, rather than assuming approval is only an administrative formality?
Grants manager
Yes. I'll identify the relevant condition or flag the question for the responsible reviewer.
Program lead
I'll keep the transfer as a proposal and avoid instructing finance to move the money yet.
Grants manager
Good. We'll clarify the restriction and approval path before making a commitment to the new activity.

conversations.title: A deliverable or an illustrative example?
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a draft grant proposal mentions six neighborhood sessions in one section and describes sessions as illustrative elsewhere; the application has not been submitted.
turns: Proposal coordinator
The draft mentions six sessions, but another section calls them illustrative. Which statement reflects our intended deliverable?
Program director
We haven't settled that distinction. I don't want the proposal to promise a fixed number accidentally.
Proposal coordinator
Could you clarify whether six is our planned commitment or simply an example of possible activity?
Program director
I need to confirm delivery capacity first. At present, neither wording should be treated as an approved commitment.
Proposal coordinator
Then I'll mark the inconsistency and ask the delivery team for the information needed to decide.
Program director
Please also check how the proposed activity connects to the donor's stated purpose and our mission.
Proposal coordinator
Yes. Mission fit and deliverable scope need separate clarification; one doesn't answer the other.
Program director
Can we keep drafting the remaining sections without submitting this ambiguous version?
Proposal coordinator
Certainly. I'll identify this as an open approval question before the application is finalized.
Program director
I'll bring a confirmed scope decision after reviewing capacity, so the final proposal says what we actually intend.

conversations.title: Unspent does not necessarily mean unrestricted
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a project has an unspent travel budget and proposes buying equipment; no review of the award's budget-change conditions has occurred.
turns: Project coordinator
The travel line has money left. Could we use it to buy equipment for the same project?
Finance partner
Possibly, but unspent money isn't necessarily unrestricted. We need to check the award's budget-change conditions.
Project coordinator
Could you clarify whether the restriction concerns the project purpose, the budget category, or both?
Finance partner
That's what the documents need to establish. I don't want to infer permission from the remaining balance.
Project coordinator
Should I get an equipment quote now, or would that imply we've approved the purchase?
Finance partner
A clearly labeled planning quote can inform discussion, but it must not become an order or commitment.
Project coordinator
Understood. I'll explain the proposed use and keep any purchasing step conditional on the review.
Finance partner
Please bring the approved budget and award reference so the restriction question is specific.
Project coordinator
I'll do that and avoid telling the team that unused travel funding is automatically available.
Finance partner
Then we can clarify the authorized route without inventing a donor permission or a spending rule.

additional_scenario.title: A donor offers equipment instead of cash
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional donor offers laptops rather than the cash requested for facilitator time. The program needs trained facilitators, and ownership, support, and any donation conditions are unknown. Hold a clarification call before accepting the offer.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the program lead. Explain the original need and ask how the proposed donation supports it.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the grants coordinator. Identify the conditions and practical responsibilities that need clarification.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Could we clarify the laptop donation's conditions before deciding whether it fits the program's actual need?
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague wants to accept immediately because the offer has a high stated value.
success_checks: Distinguish stated donation value from mission fit.
Ask about ownership, support, and restrictions without inventing answers.
Agree what must be clarified before acceptance.

conversations.title: Improvement during the program is not proof of attribution
conversations.setting: The lesson's participant outcomes improved during a program, but no comparison group or alternative explanation has been examined.
turns: Evaluation manager
Participant outcomes improved during the program. We can report that observation, but attribution remains uncertain.
Program director
Could you explain why we can't simply say the program caused the improvement?
Evaluation manager
We haven't examined a comparison group or alternative explanations, so the observed change doesn't isolate our contribution.
Program director
The baseline helps show a change over time, but it doesn't answer the cause question by itself.
Evaluation manager
Exactly. An indicator describes a measured result; a causal claim needs additional support.
Program director
I don't want our update to sound as if the improvement is meaningless, though.
Evaluation manager
It isn't meaningless. State the positive observation and the limitation together, without erasing either.
Program director
I'll say outcomes improved among participants while noting that we haven't established how much change the program caused.
Evaluation manager
Good. Our learning agenda can identify which alternative explanations and follow-up questions deserve attention.
Program director
Let's present those next questions as learning work, not as findings we already have.

conversations.title: The follow-up respondents differ from the baseline group
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: eighty people completed a baseline survey, but only forty completed follow-up; average scores rose among follow-up respondents, and nonrespondents are unexamined.
turns: Monitoring officer
Eighty people completed baseline, but only forty responded at follow-up. The reported improvement concerns those respondents.
Program lead
Can we describe the average rise as improvement across the original eighty participants?
Monitoring officer
Not without more evidence. We don't know the outcomes of those who didn't complete follow-up.
Program lead
Could nonresponse be related to how people experienced the program, or is that only a possibility?
Monitoring officer
It's a possibility worth examining, not an established explanation for the missing data.
Program lead
Then the indicator report needs both respondent counts and a clear statement about the missing outcomes.
Monitoring officer
Yes. We should also check whether the baseline comparison uses the same people where that is appropriate.
Program lead
I'll avoid claiming universal improvement or assuming nonrespondents had the same experience as respondents.
Monitoring officer
Good. The learning agenda can include a proportionate review of follow-up participation and measurement limits.
Program lead
Let's report the observed change precisely and keep the broader participant outcome question open.

conversations.title: A changed indicator breaks the comparison
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: last quarter's participation indicator counted any attendance; this quarter it counts attendance at three sessions. The dashboard shows a decline.
turns: Learning lead
The participation indicator changed from any attendance to three sessions. The quarterly figures are not directly comparable.
Program coordinator
The dashboard looks like participation fell. Could the new definition explain some of that difference?
Learning lead
It could, but we need a consistent calculation to distinguish definition effects from actual participation changes.
Program coordinator
So we shouldn't attribute the apparent decline to weaker outreach before checking the measurement basis.
Learning lead
Correct. First identify the definition change and avoid presenting it as an observed behavioral decline.
Program coordinator
Can we recalculate both periods using one definition if the underlying attendance records support it?
Learning lead
Yes. Check the available records first, and report any limits rather than filling gaps with assumptions.
Program coordinator
I'll explain the discontinuity in the dashboard and keep our outreach explanation provisional.
Learning lead
Good. Baseline consistency is essential if we want the indicator to support a meaningful comparison.
Program coordinator
I'll bring the comparable figures or a clear account of why they cannot yet be produced.

additional_scenario.title: An unusually positive interview sample
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional program's success stories come from five participants selected by facilitators for strong progress. The broader participant group has not been interviewed. Discuss what the stories can illustrate and what they cannot establish.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the evaluation officer. Explain the limited sample and avoid generalizing its experience.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the fundraising manager. Ask whether the interviews demonstrate typical outcomes.
additional_scenario.opening_line: These interviews illustrate five selected experiences, not the typical outcome across the whole program.
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague wants to describe the five stories as proof that the program works for everyone.
success_checks: Identify the selection method and sample limit.
Separate illustration from a representative outcome claim.
Agree a broader learning question without inventing an average result.

conversations.title: The visit date changed, but the transport did not
conversations.setting: The lesson's implementing partner changed a field-visit date; the community contact has not been informed and transport remains booked for the original date.
turns: Field coordinator
The visit date changed, but the community contact hasn't been told and transport still reflects the original plan.
Partner liaison
We need a clear handoff. Which communication will you own, and what should I confirm?
Field coordinator
I'll coordinate the transport review. Can you accept responsibility for contacting the community through the agreed channel?
Partner liaison
Yes. I'll explain the proposed change and check their availability rather than assume the new date works.
Field coordinator
Thank you. The partner's changed plan does not establish community agreement or a revised transport booking.
Partner liaison
Understood. I'll report the contact's response before we describe the field visit as rescheduled and confirmed.
Field coordinator
I'll check transport options and any contingency without authorizing an unreviewed change beyond my role.
Partner liaison
Let's also avoid leaving people expecting us on the original date; that could damage community trust.
Field coordinator
Agreed. Please repeat the pending actions when briefing the implementing partner.
Partner liaison
I confirm community availability; you review transport. We exchange confirmations before presenting the revised visit as settled.

conversations.title: A delivery handover with an unreadable count
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a partner's delivery sheet is legible except for the quantity of teaching kits; the receiving coordinator has not counted the kits yet.
turns: Logistics officer
The teaching-kit quantity is unreadable on the delivery sheet, and the receiving count is still pending.
Partner coordinator
Can I acknowledge the handover as complete if I can confirm that the vehicle arrived?
Logistics officer
You can acknowledge arrival, but not a verified quantity. Those are different parts of the handover.
Partner coordinator
I'll arrange the receiving count through our normal process and compare it with a clear source record.
Logistics officer
I'll request a readable dispatch copy from the sending team so you have the intended quantity.
Partner coordinator
Should I copy the most likely number into the sheet to avoid delaying our field visit?
Logistics officer
No. Keep the quantity unresolved until it is checked; a guessed count could create further confusion.
Partner coordinator
Understood. My responsibility is the receiving count, and yours is obtaining the readable dispatch record.
Logistics officer
Correct. We'll reconcile any difference and avoid calling the transfer fully verified before that happens.
Partner coordinator
I'll confirm the result and flag any remaining mismatch directly to you.

conversations.title: An interpreter request needs an acknowledged owner
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a planned community consultation requires an interpreter, but neither the nonprofit nor its implementing partner has confirmed a booking.
turns: Community engagement lead
The consultation needs an interpreter, but both teams show the booking as pending.
Partner operations coordinator
We thought your team would arrange it. Can we assign responsibility clearly before confirming the visit details?
Community engagement lead
Yes. Can your operations team check availability through the agreed booking process and report the result?
Partner operations coordinator
I can accept that coordination task, but I can't promise an interpreter until the booking is confirmed.
Community engagement lead
Understood. I'll keep the community-facing plan conditional and explain the unresolved access arrangement internally.
Partner operations coordinator
If availability doesn't match the planned visit, who will discuss a contingency with the community contact?
Community engagement lead
I'll own that discussion. We should not substitute another arrangement without checking whether it meets their needs.
Partner operations coordinator
Then I'll report confirmed availability or the specific gap, rather than mark the request handled after one email.
Community engagement lead
Exactly. A requested booking is not an accepted booking, and accessibility affects meaningful participation.
Partner operations coordinator
I'll confirm ownership now and return the actual booking status before the visit is finalized.

additional_scenario.title: A community contact asks for a different meeting place
additional_scenario.brief: For a fictional field visit, the community contact proposes moving from the school to the library. The implementing partner has not checked library availability, and the transport driver still has the school address. Agree a bounded coordination handoff.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the community liaison. Confirm that the venue change is a request, not an agreed booking.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the partner operations lead. Accept the availability check and arrange the transport update only after confirmation.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The library is the community contact's proposed venue, but its availability has not been confirmed.
additional_scenario.complication: A team member wants to tell everyone the library is booked because it was requested.
success_checks: Distinguish requested and confirmed venue status.
Assign venue checking and transport communication explicitly.
Read back the dependency before finalizing visit instructions.

conversations.title: Route a concern without unnecessary circulation
conversations.setting: In the lesson's safeguarding case, a manager discusses routing a volunteer's concern with the safeguarding focal point; no identifying details are included in this training exchange.
turns: Program manager
A volunteer raised a safeguarding concern. Could you help me use our established reporting process without unnecessary circulation?
Safeguarding focal point
Yes. Please use the designated reporting channel and keep identifying details out of this general conversation.
Program manager
Should I question other volunteers first so the incident report contains a more complete explanation?
Safeguarding focal point
Don't start an informal investigation. Follow the reporting process and distinguish what was reported from what you observed.
Program manager
Understood. I want to handle the information carefully without promising confidentiality beyond what our process allows.
Safeguarding focal point
Exactly. Use the approved explanation of confidentiality and the survivor-centered approach specified by our organization.
Program manager
Could you confirm the secure route now, so I don't delay by guessing where the concern belongs?
Safeguarding focal point
I'll direct you to the established channel and confirm how the authorized team acknowledges receipt.
Program manager
I'll provide the relevant information there and avoid adding assumptions about what happened.
Safeguarding focal point
Good. Keep the next action focused on appropriate reporting, not deciding the allegation yourself.

conversations.title: A concern sent to a shared inbox
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a fictional nonprofit receives a safeguarding message in a general project inbox; the coordinator asks its designated focal point for the approved transfer route.
turns: Project coordinator
A safeguarding message reached our shared inbox. Please confirm its approved transfer route.
Safeguarding focal point
Use our established handling process. Don't forward it to the whole project team to find an available reviewer.
Project coordinator
I won't repeat the identifying details here. Should I create my own summary and discard the original?
Safeguarding focal point
No. Follow the organization's instructions for preserving and routing the original information; don't improvise deletion or retention.
Project coordinator
Could you help me identify who acknowledges receipt, so I can confirm the concern hasn't been lost?
Safeguarding focal point
Yes. I'll connect you with the designated reporting route and its acknowledgment process.
Project coordinator
If a colleague asks what the message says, I'll explain that access is limited to the appropriate handling process.
Safeguarding focal point
Good. Confidentiality means careful information handling, not a promise that nobody else will ever need to know.
Project coordinator
I'll complete the authorized transfer and report the routing status without discussing the substance in this inbox.
Safeguarding focal point
That keeps the request actionable and protects the information from unnecessary circulation.

conversations.title: An update request without case details
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a manager knows a safeguarding concern was submitted through the approved channel but has no acknowledgment reference; they ask only about receipt, not findings.
turns: Volunteer manager
Could you confirm receipt of the concern submitted through our reporting channel? I don't have an acknowledgment reference.
Safeguarding coordinator
I can check the routing status through the authorized process. Please don't repeat the case details here.
Volunteer manager
Thank you. I'm not asking for investigative findings, only whether the report reached the responsible team.
Safeguarding coordinator
That distinction matters. An acknowledgment confirms receipt, not a conclusion or permission to share information more widely.
Volunteer manager
A team leader wants an update for the whole group. Should I summarize the allegation for them?
Safeguarding coordinator
Use our established communication guidance instead. Don't assume a general team update needs the allegation's details.
Volunteer manager
Understood. Could you tell me which approved wording applies when colleagues ask about the reporting status?
Safeguarding coordinator
I'll obtain that guidance and confirm what can appropriately be communicated within your role.
Volunteer manager
I'll wait for the authorized wording and avoid promising a particular investigation outcome or completion date.
Safeguarding coordinator
Good. I'll focus this follow-up on receipt and the appropriate communication route.

additional_scenario.title: A volunteer asks for absolute secrecy
additional_scenario.brief: In a fictional training exercise, a volunteer asks a manager to promise absolute secrecy before sharing a safeguarding concern. The organization has a designated reporting process, but its confidentiality explanation must be consulted. Practice requesting the approved explanation without eliciting case details.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the manager. Ask the safeguarding focal point how to explain information handling accurately.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the focal point. Direct the manager to the established process and avoid giving a blanket secrecy promise.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Could you help me explain our reporting process accurately before I make any promise about confidentiality?
additional_scenario.complication: The manager fears that admitting limits will sound uncaring.
success_checks: Use respectful language without promising absolute secrecy.
Keep identifying details out of the practice exchange.
Agree the approved reporting and confidentiality explanation as the next step.

conversations.title: Enthusiasm beyond the agreed role
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case aligned with the lesson: a reception volunteer trained to book appointments offers to conduct eligibility interviews alone; those interviews belong to the trained program team.
turns: Volunteer supervisor
You offered to conduct eligibility interviews alone, but your agreed reception role covers appointment booking.
Reception volunteer
I wanted to help with the queue. I thought listening to an interview meant I could conduct one.
Volunteer supervisor
Observing helps you learn, but it does not establish the training or authorization this task requires.
Reception volunteer
I see. I could give visitors an inaccurate impression that I am making an official assessment.
Volunteer supervisor
Exactly. Please continue booking appointments and refer eligibility questions to the trained program team.
Reception volunteer
Can I still ask about developing my volunteer role without taking on those interviews now?
Volunteer supervisor
Certainly. We can discuss appropriate training and supervision with the program lead, without promising a role change.
Reception volunteer
For this shift, I will manage bookings and ask the program team to handle interview requests.
Volunteer supervisor
Good. If the queue grows, tell me so we can coordinate support within the agreed arrangements.
Reception volunteer
I will. I will not conduct interviews independently, and I will raise the queue issue with you.

conversations.title: A helpful answer that went beyond training
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a reception volunteer answered a visitor's eligibility question despite being trained only to explain appointment booking; no eligibility decision is established.
turns: Volunteer supervisor
You told the visitor they were eligible, although your current role covers appointment booking, not eligibility assessment.
Reception volunteer
I recognized one condition from the leaflet and assumed that was enough. I should have checked.
Volunteer supervisor
That answer may create an expectation of approval. The program team needs to assess the relevant information.
Reception volunteer
Should I contact the visitor myself and say they are not eligible instead?
Volunteer supervisor
No. That would make another unsupported decision. I will arrange an appropriate correction with the program team.
Reception volunteer
Understood. What should I say when another visitor asks whether meeting one condition guarantees approval?
Volunteer supervisor
Explain that the authorized team assesses eligibility, and offer to help with the appointment process.
Reception volunteer
I can say, I can help you book, but the program team must answer the eligibility question.
Volunteer supervisor
Exactly. Let's practice two more examples together before you return to the reception desk.
Reception volunteer
Yes. I will keep my answers within booking and ask for support when a question goes beyond it.

conversations.title: A shift handover missing the unresolved request
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a volunteer's handover omitted an unresolved accessible-appointment request, so the receiving coordinator could not follow up without asking the visitor again.
turns: Shift supervisor
Your handover listed completed tasks but omitted the accessible-appointment request the next coordinator needed.
Reception volunteer
I thought the handover covered only finished work. I did not realize pending requests belonged there too.
Shift supervisor
Without that action, the coordinator had to ask the visitor to explain the request again.
Reception volunteer
I understand the effect. Should I include every detail from the visitor's conversation next time?
Shift supervisor
No. Use the approved record and share only what the receiving role needs to take the next action.
Reception volunteer
Then I should identify the outstanding appointment request and ask who will accept the follow-up.
Shift supervisor
Exactly. End the handover with a spoken check of pending actions and the person responsible.
Reception volunteer
For my next shift change, I will ask the coordinator to confirm the outstanding action before I leave.
Shift supervisor
Good. I will observe that handover and help if the responsibility or information is unclear.
Reception volunteer
Thank you. I will distinguish completed work from requests still needing attention and confirm the receiving owner.

additional_scenario.title: A volunteer changes the appointment order
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional reception volunteer rearranged appointment order to help a late arrival without consulting the supervisor. Two people then received conflicting instructions. The supervisor can consult the applicable scheduling process. Give feedback directly to the volunteer and agree what they will do next time.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the supervisor. Describe the observed change and its effect, then ask the volunteer to consult before changing appointment order.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the reception volunteer. Explain your intention, respond to the conflicting instructions, and agree a specific consultation step without making another unauthorized change.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Changing the appointment order without checking created conflicting instructions for two visitors.
additional_scenario.complication: The volunteer argues that helping the late arrival justified the change, even though the other visitors were affected.
success_checks: Acknowledge the intention without dismissing the observed effect.
Explain and respond to the role boundary directly.
Have the volunteer state a specific consultation step for the next similar situation.

conversations.title: A striking statistic without a source
conversations.setting: The lesson's fundraising draft uses an alarming statistic with no source or date, and the campaign team wants to publish immediately.
turns: Campaign editor
The fundraising draft contains an alarming statistic, but its source and date are missing.
Advocacy lead
It would give the campaign urgency. Can we keep it while someone looks for the reference?
Campaign editor
We shouldn't publish it as established evidence before verification. Urgency doesn't establish accuracy or current relevance.
Advocacy lead
Could we qualify it with reportedly rather than delay the whole message?
Campaign editor
That word doesn't supply a source. We need to verify the claim or use wording supported by known information.
Advocacy lead
Agreed. We should also consider whether the language respects the dignity of the people described.
Campaign editor
Yes. An unsupported dramatic claim can misrepresent both their circumstances and our evidence.
Advocacy lead
I'll ask the draft owner for the original source, date, and relevant population before using the figure.
Campaign editor
I'll keep the statistic out of the publish-ready version until the appropriate review is complete.
Advocacy lead
Then we can discuss an accurate campaign message without treating an unverified number as essential.

conversations.title: A participant quotation with an uncertain permission scope
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a nonprofit has a participant quotation from an internal learning interview; permission for a public advocacy campaign has not been confirmed.
turns: Advocacy producer
This interview quotation is powerful, but we haven't confirmed permission to use it in the public campaign.
Program communications lead
The participant agreed to the interview. Doesn't that establish permission to publish their words more widely?
Advocacy producer
Not from the information we have. The interview agreement and public-use permission need to be checked.
Program communications lead
Then I shouldn't describe the quotation as cleared just because it appears in our internal report.
Advocacy producer
Correct. We also need to preserve context and dignity, rather than select wording only for emotional effect.
Program communications lead
Could we anonymize it and assume that removes the permission question?
Advocacy producer
No. Anonymization doesn't establish the scope of the original agreement. Use the organization's review process.
Program communications lead
I'll ask the responsible colleague to verify permission and context without contacting the participant outside that process.
Advocacy producer
Good. Meanwhile, keep the quotation out of the approved campaign assets and identify the unresolved question.
Program communications lead
I'll do that and avoid claiming the quotation represents every participant's experience.

conversations.title: A campaign photograph from another year
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: an advocacy draft pairs a current event appeal with a clearly dated photograph from three years earlier; the caption omits the date.
turns: Visual communications editor
The photograph is from three years ago, but the current-event appeal doesn't identify that date.
Campaign manager
Could readers assume it shows the present event, even though the photograph itself is genuine?
Visual communications editor
Yes. A real image can still create an unsupported impression when the context is missing.
Campaign manager
Then our issue isn't proving the photograph is fake; it's accurately describing what it shows.
Visual communications editor
Exactly. We need the known date and context visible, alongside the usual permissions and dignity review.
Campaign manager
Would calling it illustrative be enough without explaining that it comes from a different period?
Visual communications editor
Let's avoid relying on an ambiguous label. The caption should not encourage a current-event interpretation we cannot support.
Campaign manager
I'll ask for a contextually accurate asset or a clear caption, rather than suggest the image documents today's conditions.
Visual communications editor
Good. Keep the campaign's verified claims separate from what the older photograph can establish.
Campaign manager
We'll review the revised pairing before publication so the appeal remains accurate as well as compelling.

additional_scenario.title: An advocacy headline turns correlation into cause
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional report finds that service use and school attendance rose during the same year. A campaign headline says the service caused the attendance increase. No causal analysis is supplied. Discuss a supported headline claim aloud.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the advocacy lead. Explain the known concurrent changes without claiming causation.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the campaign editor. Ask which source and scope should accompany the statement.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The report shows both measures rose, but it doesn't establish that our service caused the attendance increase.
additional_scenario.complication: A campaign partner says the causal headline will attract more attention.
success_checks: Distinguish concurrent observations from a causal finding.
Request the report's missing source and scope details before agreeing a final headline.
Agree accurate spoken wording for the claim before publication review.

conversations.title: Restricted balances are not automatically available reserves
conversations.setting: The lesson's board considers reserves or reduced program activity during a funding gap; some funds are restricted and no detailed forecast is supplied.
turns: Board finance chair
We need to compare using reserves with reducing program activity during the funding gap.
Executive director
The bank balance looks sufficient, but some funds are restricted. We shouldn't treat all cash as available reserves.
Board finance chair
Agreed. Can we compare both scenarios over the same period and separate usable funds from restricted balances?
Executive director
Yes. Using available reserves may preserve activity temporarily, while reducing activity changes delivery and may conserve cash.
Board finance chair
Neither option should be presented as automatically safer without the cash forecast and program implications.
Executive director
Correct. We also need to identify which assumptions drive the cash runway in each scenario.
Board finance chair
Could the forecast include expected donations as guaranteed receipts to make the gap look manageable?
Executive director
No. Unconfirmed funding should remain an assumption, not a certainty in the base figures.
Board finance chair
I'll ask for a consistent comparison and the relevant restrictions before the board makes its decision.
Executive director
I'll bring the program tradeoffs and forecast uncertainties, keeping this as a governance discussion rather than a predetermined answer.

conversations.title: A bridge donation that has not been pledged
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a nonprofit compares maintaining four weekly sessions with reducing to two; a possible donor contribution is under discussion but not pledged.
turns: Executive director
We can model four weekly sessions or two, but the possible donor contribution is not pledged.
Board treasurer
Then neither scenario should count that contribution as a confirmed source of cash.
Executive director
Agreed. The reduced schedule lowers activity, while maintaining four sessions preserves current access for now.
Board treasurer
What else needs comparison besides the immediate cash use in each scenario?
Executive director
Participant continuity, staffing implications, and whether any funding restrictions affect the planned spending.
Board treasurer
Could we calculate cash runway only for the reduced schedule because that option appears more cautious?
Executive director
We should calculate both using the same period and assumptions, so the board can see the actual tradeoff.
Board treasurer
Yes. And any donor-funded variant should be labeled conditional on a contribution that isn't yet committed.
Executive director
I'll present the two operating scenarios and keep potential funding separate from confirmed resources.
Board treasurer
That gives board governance a clearer basis without pretending the preferred option has no service consequences.

conversations.title: A reserve-funded restart or a gradual reopening
conversations.setting: Separate fictional case: a nonprofit considers restarting all three community groups together or reopening one first; restart costs and facilitator availability are not yet confirmed.
turns: Board program chair
Restarting all three groups restores activity sooner, whereas reopening one first creates a smaller initial commitment.
Operations director
That's the broad distinction, but restart costs and facilitator availability still need confirmation for both scenarios.
Board program chair
Could a smaller restart also postpone access for participants in the other two groups?
Operations director
Yes, that is a program tradeoff to discuss, not something the reserve calculation captures by itself.
Board program chair
Then the comparison should include service access alongside cash use and operational readiness.
Operations director
Agreed. We shouldn't describe either option as funded or staffed until the relevant information is verified.
Board program chair
What common time horizon would let the board compare the reserve effect fairly?
Operations director
Let's agree that with finance and apply it to both options rather than select whichever period favors one.
Board program chair
I'll request the consistent forecast and ask the program team to explain the access implications.
Operations director
I'll obtain readiness information so the board sees both the benefits and the limitations of each restart plan.

additional_scenario.title: A lease extension during a funding gap
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional nonprofit can discuss a six-month office extension or moving to shared space. The shared-space fee is lower, but moving costs and suitability for confidential appointments are unassessed. Compare the options over six months for a board discussion.
additional_scenario.role_a: You are the operations director. Identify known fees and missing operational costs.
additional_scenario.role_b: You are the board finance chair. Ask about reserve use and the effect on service delivery.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The shared-space fee is lower, but we haven't included moving costs or checked whether appointments can be held appropriately.
additional_scenario.complication: A board member calls the fee difference a confirmed saving.
success_checks: Use the same six-month comparison period.
Distinguish a lower fee from verified total savings.
State service and cash tradeoffs and request the missing evidence.
